story.name: ジョニーの たび
story.title: The Slow Ferry
story.line: ジョニーが せとないかいの フェリーの はなしを します
story.ja: ジョニーは絵はがきを手に、瀬戸内海へ。島から島へ、のんびり進む小さなフェリーに乗る。レモン畑、港の猫、桟橋の大きな水玉のかぼちゃ。漁師のおじいさんにみかんをもらい、畳の席で昼寝をして、降りる港を3回も乗り過ごす。でも、いちばんいい間違いだった。

segments.en: On the third night, there was no wind at all. The sea was flat and silver under the moon, which, Gulliver said, was perfect for a ferry story.
Cherry had come down with a bag of marshmallows to roast, and Dom was back, still in his running shorts, even though it was cold.
So you went to Japan, just because of a postcard? Like, that's it? That's the whole reason?
My dear, a postcard is the best reason there is. Most of my trips start with worse ones.
He got a job on a ship heading for Japan, peeling potatoes in the kitchen. Six weeks of potatoes, he said. He still dreams about them.
He got off in a little port town on the coast. The streets went steeply up the hill, and there were cats sleeping on almost every step.
One of them followed me all the way to the ferry. Big orange fellow. I think he wanted my sandwich more than my company.
The ferry was small and white, just like the one in the postcard. It wasn't fast. It wasn't fancy. It was in no rush to get anywhere.
It went from island to island, stopping at tiny piers where a few people got off and a few people got on, and somebody always waved.
Inside, there was a room with a tatami floor, and people just lay down on it.
Grandparents, students, a man in a suit with his shoes lined up neatly by the door.
Wait, people just sleep on the floor? On the ferry? That's awesome. I'd be out in, like, two minutes.
That's the thing. I meant to stay awake. I really did. I had my postcard out and everything.
The islands slid past the windows, green and soft and round, with lemon trees growing in rows down the hillsides, right to the water.
On one island, a giant yellow pumpkin with black polka dots sat at the end of a pier, like it was waiting for a boat too.
A giant pumpkin? With polka dots? Okay, now I know you're just messing with us.
It's art! Famous art! People come from all over the world just to take a picture with it.
At the next stop, an old fisherman got on with a bucket and sat down next to Gulliver.
He didn't say much. He just smiled and handed him a mikan.
Then another mikan. Then a third. By the time they had passed two islands, Gulliver had a little pile of orange peels on his lap.
We didn't share a language, him and me. But we shared a lot of fruit. I think that counts for something.
And then, with the sun on the tatami and the engine humming under the floor, Gulliver lay down, just to rest his eyes for a moment.
When he opened them again, the ferry was back where it started. He had missed his stop.
Oh, man. That's rough. So what'd you do? Just get off and try again tomorrow?
Try again tomorrow? Nonsense. I stayed on and went right back the other way. And then I fell asleep again.
He missed his stop three times that day. Back and forth, back and forth, across the same calm water.
The ferry crew started to recognize him. On the last trip, one of them brought him a cup of green tea without being asked.
Honestly, it was the best mistake I've ever made. I saw every island twice, and I've never slept better in my life.
Okay, I'll admit it, that's kind of perfect. So did you ever get off the boat?
Eventually. At the very last port, as the sun went down, there was a big ship in the harbor with a sign. It said, Los Angeles.
And Gulliver, who never could say no to a sign, picked up his bag and walked straight toward it.
Dom was already yawning. Cherry ate the last marshmallow. And the moon sat on the flat, silver sea, as calm as a ferry with nowhere special to be.

predict.ask: アメリカで ジョニーは どこに いく？
choices: He takes a cooking job on a cruise ship.
He gets lost in a big city and sleeps in a park.
He rides with a truck driver and stops at a diner in the desert.
predict.ja: トラックの運転手と砂漠を走り、ダイナーに寄る。
